text:
perf-bot: 🚨 nightly-perf alert: small-batch p95 latency up 32% vs baseline on gpu-pool-a (commit: a1b2c3d). Artifacts: https://ci.redwood/example/1764207890/artifacts

maria: saw it. any obvious infra noise?

jia: not from infra dashboards, no node restarts, GPU utilization normal. attaching perf diff: https://perf.redwood/reports/1764207890

ravi: ok I'll start a quick bisect across the last 6 commits. ping me if you want a hand.

sam: throwing flamegraph here — https://prof.redwood/fg/1764207890 (top shows more time in attention kernel)

lily: @ravi fyi the PR that touched scheduler was merged last night (PR #4785, author: oz). commit a1b2c3d is in that chain.

ravi: thanks. starting bisection: running bench suite locally against a1b2c3d and parent. cmd I'm using: `./scripts/run_micro_bench.sh --suite=small-batch --iters=50 --device=gpu`

jia: if you need exact env, use docker image `redwood/runtime:nightly-2026-03-15` — that matches CI.

perf-bot: test artifacts uploaded: s3://redwood-ci/nightly/1764207890/{bench.log,profiles.tgz}

sam: paste of the top error lines from bench.log:```
[2026-03-15T04:12:03Z] step=decode token=512 ms=1.2
[2026-03-15T04:12:03Z] step=attn kernel=flash_attn ms=14.8
[2026-03-15T04:12:03Z] step=attn kernel=flash_attn ms=32.1
[2026-03-15T04:12:03Z] p95=48.3ms p99=92.1ms
```

oz: that looks like the attention kernel regressed. PR #4785 didn't touch kernels but changed scheduler pacing — could expose a hot path.

maria: @ravi can you confirm whether regression is present if we pin the model backend to v2-kernel (older kernels)? quick test: set `REDBWD_KERNEL_TAG=v2-kernel` and rerun small-batch.

ravi: running that now locally, will post results. ETA ~12m.

(12 minutes later)
ravi: pinned to v2-kernel -> p95 back to 36ms (down from 48). looks like change in runtime picks up newer kernel by default.

lily: interesting. maybe scheduler change nudges micro-batching that triggers a different kernel code path.

sam: can someone grab the kernel selection logs from the failing CI run? `grep -i "selected kernel" bench.log` should show which kernel was used per layer.

jia: I pulled them: `selected kernel: flash_attn_v3 (heuristic=seq_len>256 && batch<8)`. baseline run selected `flash_attn_v2`

oz: that heuristic was updated in runtime/heuristics last week (commit d4e5f6). cc @maria for rollback/discussion.

maria: next steps: 1) open revert PR for heuristics commit d4e5f6 with a note to owners; 2) add an explicit kernel pin in nightly CI until we fix; 3) run a full bisect if needed. who wants the revert PR? @oz?

oz: I can open the revert PR now, will target canary branch and include perf numbers.

ravi: meanwhile I'll create a minimal repro docker image and a flamegraph that shows layer-level differences, will upload to the artifacts link.

sam: tagging perf-oncall @lily — please loop in SRE if we need to hotfix kernel rollout.

lily: will do; pinging infra-team. also recommend we add a `--kernel=force:v2` flag for quick CI override.

maria: thanks all. if revert PR merges and CI passes, we can promote to nightly stable. If not, we escalate to postmortem. please post status updates here. :thumbsup:

(30 minutes later)

oz: opened revert PR: https://github.com/redwood/runtime/pull/4801 — includes bench numbers and backout of d4e5f6. requesting review from @sam @maria

perf-bot: nightly-perf update: rerun with kernel pin succeeded, p95 delta now within +/-2% baseline. CI green.

maria: nice. let's keep the pin in CI for 24h and follow up with a deeper investigation into scheduler heuristics. created a ticket: https://issues.redwood/RT-9921

ravi: adding notes to the ticket with repro steps and command used.

jia: closing out oncall handoff — if anything else flares, re-open thread. good job y'all.
